recommendations.rationale: MIR-ATR has a supplied precedent for water content in petroleum and suits liquid or soft-solid contact measurements. It is the single method to test first for water changes.
recommendations.conditions: Use only if the stream is a liquid or paste that can wet the ATR crystal and if the water level is within the method's usable range, which is unknown.

suitability of analyzed samples for ATR measurements, which is true for liquid or soft solid samples and their components, allowing a tight contact with the probe head.

recommendations.rationale: NIR transmission/transflection is the most common online fiber method and can sample a defined path through clear liquids. It is a useful cross-check against MIR-ATR, but its fit depends on low scattering and a controlled pathlength.
recommendations.conditions: Test only if the stream is transparent or semi-transparent and a pathlength in the 1-10 mm range is practical.

citations.quote: Near-IR vibrational spectroscopy (NIR) is the most common online analysis method performed using fiber optic probes.
Transmission is the preferred method for transparent or semi-transparent liquids, such as skim milk, whey, or permeate.
the precise control of the optical pathlength (usually 1 - 10 mm)

recommendations.rationale: If single-method tests show that MIR-ATR misses free or emulsified water while NIR sees bulk water, the two methods may be complementary and should be compared with the best single method. Any gain is a hypothesis, not an established result.
recommendations.conditions: Only after single-method tests, and only if both methods can view the same stream location and their data can be synchronised.

measurement_concept.probe_and_geometry: Start with an ATR fiber probe in contact with the liquid or soft-solid stream; compare with a NIR transmission or transflection probe only if the stream is clear enough and a controlled pathlength is practical.
measurement_concept.location: Probe at the process point; analyzer outside the process area, with the fiber route and length still to be defined.
measurement_concept.fiber_link: Fiber family depends on the chosen method; MIR needs a fiber that transmits the mid-IR range, while NIR can use silica fibers. No link length is stated here.

spectral_ranges.statement: Nominal MIR range is 4000-400 cm-1; the usable range depends on the instrument, fiber and ATR probe selected.

citations.quote: Vibrational spectroscopy in the mid-IR range (4000-400 cm-1) is one of the most informative methods of chemical analysis.

spectral_ranges.statement: Nominal NIR range is 780-2500 nm; the usable range depends on the instrument, fiber and probe selected.

citations.quote: NIR spectra (780-2500 nm) contain predominantly overtones and component bands of fundamental vibrations

risks.risk: The stream may be opaque, emulsified or contain free water, so a surface ATR reading may not represent the bulk and NIR transmission may fail.
Water concentration may be below the detection capability of the chosen method; the sources give no detection limit for this stream.
The customer's laboratory water determination may not be independent or comparable enough to serve as a reference.
The analyzer may be outside the process area but the required fiber length, routing, temperature and safety conditions are unknown and could rule out a configuration.

solution_options.performance_fit: only if single methods miss fractions
solution_options.cost_drivers: two spectrometers, two probes, synchronisation, fusion modelling
solution_options.fusion_note: Low-level fusion of synchronised MIR-ATR and NIR transmission/transflection spectra, with block scaling so neither method dominates. Both probes must view the same stream volume and time step; each method needs its own calibration. The fused model must beat the best single method on held-out runs, otherwise drop the extra method.

chemometrics_note: MIR-ATR and NIR water calibrations are matrix-specific; build them on representative petroleum samples and re-check after stream composition changes.
realtime_tracking_note: The aim is earlier notice of water changes; define whether the measurement must be continuous, time-resolved or a short cycle, because that sets the acquisition and synchronisation needs.
future_direction: If single-method tests show different water fractions are missed, a combined MIR-ATR/NIR probe or a dedicated water sensor could be considered later.

proposal.what_would_change_it: If the stream is opaque or emulsified, or if the water range is outside MIR-ATR capability, NIR or the combined option would move ahead; if the laboratory reference is unsuitable, the comparison cannot decide.
proposal.next_step: Run the first comparison on representative samples against the laboratory water method, starting with MIR-ATR and NIR as separate single-method tests.

brief_answer: Start with a single-method MIR-ATR test, because a supplied example shows water content in petroleum measured with ATR probes; compare it with NIR transmission/transflection only if the stream is clear enough. The first experiment should compare both against your laboratory water method on representative samples. Still open are the water range and phase, stream state, required response time, and the fiber route from process to analyzer.
